ui.opt.timeout: Timeout — how long one check may take before it counts as failed
ui.opt.retry: Retry interval — how soon to check again after a failure
ui.opt.attempts: Attempts — failed checks in a row before it is a problem
ui.opt.recover-attempts: Recovery attempts — good checks in a row before it counts as recovered
ui.opt.degraded: Slow threshold — slower than this is shown as degraded
ui.opt.scope: Network scope — lan or wan; wan checks are held back while this host's own internet is down
ui.opt.authorized: Authorized — UDP checks only: yes when the target is your own device. DNS, NTP and SNMP replies can be abused for reflection attacks; without it the configuration shows a warning
ui.opt.family: IP version — 4 or 6, to check over one of them only
ui.opt.on-filtered: When this host's firewall blocks — fail (default) or abstain when this host's own firewall refuses to send the request. A remote firewall that drops it shows as a timeout instead
ui.opt.parent: Parent — the monitor this one sits behind, such as the switch or router in front of it; while the parent is down, this one's failures are recorded but not alerted
ui.opt.aa: Authoritative only — yes accepts only answers with the AA bit set
ui.opt.allow-metadata: Allow cloud metadata — yes lets the check reach an address such as 169.254.169.254
ui.opt.expect-len: Expected length — the reply must be this many bytes
ui.opt.fallback: TCP fallback — when this host cannot send ICMP, knock on TCP 443, 80 and 22 instead (default); off turns it off
ui.opt.host-check: Host check — when the UDP port stays silent, count it as open only while the host answers a ping; off accepts silence alone
ui.opt.max-offset: Largest clock offset — fail when the server's clock differs from this host's by more than this, e.g. 500ms
ui.opt.max-stratum: Highest stratum — fail when the NTP stratum is above this (default 15)
ui.opt.min-answers: Fewest answers — fail with fewer answer records than this
ui.opt.retransmit: Retransmissions — how often an unanswered UDP request is sent again within one check (0–5, default 1)
ui.opt.src-port: Source port — send from this local port, for devices that only answer a fixed source port
ui.opt.template: Protocol template — which protocol to speak, such as dns, ntp, snmp or raw; by default the port decides
ui.opt.cert-days: Certificate warning days — degraded when the certificate expires within this many days
ui.opt.cert-critical-days: Certificate critical days — failed when the certificate expires within this many days
ui.opt.handler: Event handler — script from the check-scripts directory run on each state change
ui.opt.expect: Expected answer — status codes for HTTP (200-399), text or value for other checks
ui.opt.keyword: Keyword — the page must contain this text
ui.opt.keyword-regex: Keyword pattern — the page must match this regular expression
ui.opt.absent: Must not contain — the check fails when the page contains this text
ui.opt.json-path: JSON path — the value to check in a JSON reply, such as $.status
ui.opt.json-expect: JSON expected — the value at the JSON path must equal this
ui.opt.json-expect-num: JSON number check — a comparison such as < 500 for the value at the JSON path
ui.opt.body: Request body — sent with POST or PUT
ui.opt.host: Host header — the name sent to the server, for a target given as an address
ui.opt.basic: Basic login — user:password for HTTP basic authentication
ui.opt.bearer: Bearer token — sent as Authorization: Bearer …
ui.opt.proxy: Proxy — HTTP proxy to go through
ui.opt.no-follow: Do not follow redirects — yes to check the redirect itself
ui.opt.insecure: Skip certificate check — yes accepts any certificate (expiry is still watched)
ui.opt.header.Authorization: Request header — header.Name=value adds a header
ui.opt.send: Send — text sent after connecting (\r\n for line breaks)
ui.opt.send-hex: Send (hex) — bytes sent after connecting, in hexadecimal
ui.opt.expect-hex: Expected bytes (hex) — the reply must start with these bytes
ui.opt.expect-regex: Expected pattern — the reply must match this regular expression
ui.opt.tls: TLS — yes to connect with TLS and watch the certificate
ui.opt.servername: TLS server name — the name sent in TLS (SNI)
ui.opt.count: Ping count — echo requests per check
ui.opt.loss: Loss threshold — percent lost before it fails
ui.opt.rtt: Round-trip limit — slower replies count as degraded
ui.opt.query: Query name — the name to look up
ui.opt.qtype: Record type — A, AAAA, MX, TXT …
ui.opt.recurse: Recursion — no to ask an authoritative server directly
ui.opt.community: SNMP community — v1/v2c password; keep it in a secret
ui.opt.version: Protocol version — such as 2c or 3 for SNMP
ui.opt.oid: OID — the SNMP object to read
ui.opt.expect-program: RPC program — the program number the portmapper must list
ui.opt.accept-from: Accept replies from — connected (default) or any source address
ui.opt.expect-all: Expect all — every one of these addresses must be in the answer
ui.opt.password: Password — keep it in a secret
ui.opt.role: Redis role — master, replica or sentinel the server must have
ui.opt.ssl: SSL — yes to connect with TLS
ui.opt.service: gRPC service — the service name for the health check
ui.opt.socket: Docker socket — path of the Docker socket
ui.opt.days: Warning days — degraded when the domain expires within this many days
ui.opt.critical-days: Critical days — failed when the domain expires within this many days
ui.opt.rdap: RDAP server — address of the RDAP service to ask
ui.opt.whois: WHOIS server — server to ask instead of RDAP
ui.opt.expect-num: Number check — a comparison such as > 0 for the value read
ui.opt.period: Expected every — how often the push should arrive
ui.opt.grace: Grace — how late a push may be before it is a problem
ui.mon.options_hint2: Settings beyond the fields above, such as the HTTP method, an expected status code or a keyword. Pick one from the list; its meaning and an example are shown. Custom takes any option of the configuration file.
ui.mon.type_hint.HTTP: Requests a URL and checks the status code, optionally a keyword or JSON value, and the certificate.
ui.mon.type_hint.TCP: Connects to a port; can send a string and expect a reply, or check TLS.
ui.mon.type_hint.PING: ICMP echo; reports loss and round-trip time.
ui.mon.type_hint.UDP: Speaks the real protocol of well-known UDP services (DNS, NTP, SNMP, …) by keyword, or a raw payload.
ui.mon.type_hint.DNS: Asks a DNS server for a name and checks the answer.
ui.mon.type_hint.NTP: Asks a time server and checks that it answers and its offset.
ui.mon.type_hint.SNMP: Reads an OID with SNMP v1/v2c (v3 discovery without credentials).
ui.mon.type_hint.SYSLOG: Sends a syslog test message (UDP cannot confirm delivery: weak check).
ui.mon.type_hint.PUSH: Waits for your job to call a URL; alerts when it stops calling.
ui.mon.target_hint.DNS: DNS server to ask; set query=name
ui.mon.target_hint.SNMP: Device address; set community and oid

ui.ob.title: Get started
ui.ob.s1_hint: One per line: a URL, host:port, host:keyword or ping host.
ui.ob.s2_hint: Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, Telegram, Slack, email or a webhook — then send a test message.
ui.ob.s3_hint: No new team is needed: pick, for the built-in administrators' team, which channels it is told through.
ui.why.title: Notifications
ui.why.paused: Paused: not checked and not notified.
ui.why.maint: In a maintenance window: failures are not notified and not counted.
ui.why.parent: Its parent {parent} is down: only the parent alerts.
ui.why.local: This host's own network is down: judgement is held, and you get one summary instead of an alert per target.
ui.why.unknown: Cannot be judged ({reason}): not counted as a failure.
ui.why.partial: Each site checks and alerts independently. Shared observations are informational only.
ui.why.slow: Slow is not down: no failure alert.
ui.why.soft: Soft state {attempt}/{max}: it alerts after {max} failures in a row.
ui.why.acked: Acknowledged by {who}: no more reminders; you still hear when it recovers.
ui.why.capped: Notification limit of {max} reached: no more reminders.
ui.why.no_channels: Not notified: policy {policy} has no channels.
ui.why.queued: The notification is queued or delayed by the policy.
ui.mon.type_hint.REDIS: Logs in when password= is given and expects PONG; role=master or replica checks replication.
ui.mon.type_hint.POSTGRES: Logs in with user= and password= (md5 or SCRAM) and runs SELECT 1; without credentials, proves the server answers. ssl=yes for SSL.
ui.mon.type_hint.MYSQL: Logs in with user= and password= and sends a ping; without credentials, reads the server greeting. ssl=yes for SSL.
ui.mon.type_hint.GRPC: Calls the standard gRPC health check (grpc.health.v1) and expects SERVING; service= asks about one service, tls=yes for TLS.
ui.mon.type_hint.DOCKER: Checks a container on each probing node through its Docker socket: running, and healthy if it has a health check.
ui.ch.period_hint: Only send inside this time period (PERIOD record); !name sends only outside it.
ui.ch.members_hint: Channel names, comma separated; all of them are notified at once.
ui.import.nagios_intro: Choose the Nagios object files (hosts, services, commands, contacts, time periods; several at once). Templates are resolved; plugins without a built-in equivalent become EXEC checks that need the plugin in the check-scripts directory.
ui.pub.link_invalid: This link is no longer valid.
ui.notice.intro: Announcements appear on the public status page; subscribers can be e-mailed. Status pages are STATUSPAGE records in monitors.conf (domain= for an own host name, subscribe=CHANNEL for e-mail subscriptions).
ui.notice.title: Title
ui.notice.no_pages_hint: Add a STATUSPAGE record to monitors.conf, e.g. public IN STATUSPAGE "Service status" select="tag:public".
ui.import.user.quota: not added: the licence's account limit is reached
ui.reg.over_quota: over the licence: nothing is switched off, but no more can be added
ui.err.record_changed: Someone else changed this in the meantime. Reload to see their version, then make your change again.
ui.uptime.coverage: Watched for only {pct} of this window so far: too little for an uptime figure.
ui.node.needs_upgrade: Too old for {n} checks: upgrade it
ui.dir.intro: Everyone who signs in or receives alerts. E-mail and SMS go only to active people: people on leave, transferred or gone, addresses that keep bouncing and addresses not listed are skipped.
ui.dir.add_login_hint: Signs in to the console and can receive alerts
ui.dir.add_contact_hint: Does not sign in, such as an on-call phone or an outside partner
ui.user.username_hint: The name typed to sign in; it cannot be changed later
ui.user.delete_login_confirm: Delete the login of {name}? They stay in the user list and still receive alerts.
ui.dir.name: Name
ui.dir.handle_hint: Use it as @handle in a channel instead of typing the address.
ui.dir.username_hint: When the person leaves, this login is disabled too.
ui.dir.left_confirm: {name} left? Nothing will be sent to their addresses any more and their login stops working.
ui.dir.none_hint: Add the people who receive alerts, or import the addresses your channels already use.
ui.dir.unknown_banner: Addresses used by channels but not in the directory, so not sent to: {n}
ui.dir.bounce_rule: An address refused as nonexistent {n} times is no longer sent to.
ui.dir.bounce_off: Bounced addresses are still sent to (contacts.bounce-threshold is 0).
ui.dir.clear_hint: Fixed it? Clear the count and send to it again.
ui.dir.new_intro: These addresses are not in the contact directory. Add them, so they are kept up to date when people leave?
ui.dir.nav_dot: Some channels have recipients to check: {n}
ui.dir.issue.unknown_handle: {address} is not in the directory: nothing is sent for it
ui.dir.issue.bouncing: {address} was refused as nonexistent {n} times: skipped
ui.dir.issue.no_address: {person} has no address of this kind
ui.dir.issue.unknown_address: {address} is not in the directory: not sent to
ui.chg.intro: Announce planned work: the people concerned are told, reminded before it starts and told how it ended; the monitors it touches are in maintenance during the window.
ui.chg.title: Title
ui.chg.select_hint: Monitor filter (group:, tag:, name:…); they are held in maintenance during the window.
ui.chg.notify_resched: Tell them about the new time
ui.chg.note_hint: Shown in the receipt: what was done, what to watch.
ui.chg.templates_hint2: The notices a planned change sends. Each one says when it goes out and shows what it looks like; Edit changes its title and text. A line whose names are all empty is left out, so “Impact: …” disappears for a change without an impact.
ui.chg.lines_hint: Click a name to insert it where the cursor is (title or text). Write plain lines; a line whose names are all empty is left out.
ui.chg.pv_short: Example without impact, description or note
ui.chg.when.announced: Sent when the change is announced.
ui.chg.when.rescheduled: Sent when its time is changed.
ui.chg.when.remind: Sent shortly before it starts, as a reminder.
ui.chg.when.started: Sent when the change window begins; its monitors go into maintenance.
ui.chg.when.overdue: Sent when the window has ended but the change is not marked done or rolled back.
ui.chg.when.done: Sent when the change is marked done.
ui.chg.when.rolled_back: Sent when the change is marked rolled back.
ui.chg.when.cancelled: Sent when the change is cancelled.
ui.chg.var.Title: Change title
ui.chg.templates_hint: Go templates: {{.Title}}, {{.Start}}, {{.End}}, {{.Duration}}, {{.Impact}}, {{.Description}}, {{.Monitors}}, {{.In}}, {{.Note}}, {{.By}}, {{.Now}}. Empty restores the built-in text.
ui.chg.none_hint: Announce planned work so the people concerned know before it happens.
ui.mon.type_hint.DOMAIN: Watches when the domain's registration expires (RDAP, or WHOIS where there is none): degraded inside days= (30), failing inside critical-days= (7). Checked every 6 hours.
ui.exp.title: Certificate validity
ui.exp.intro: Every TLS certificate and domain registration the checks watch, soonest first.
ui.exp.none_hint: HTTP and TLS checks report their certificates; a DOMAIN check watches a domain's registration.
ui.ob.s4_hint: Put every e-mail address and phone number in the contact directory, so people who leave stop getting alerts.
ui.ob.s5_hint: Show customers and colleagues what works, and post maintenance notices.
ui.notice.page_title_hint: Shown at the top of the status page; change it here at any time. For example: {example}
ui.notice.page_select_hint: A monitor filter: group:public shows the monitors with group=public; type:HTTP all web checks.
ui.mon.host_hint: Name or IP address, without a port.
ui.mon.port_required: Required: the port to connect to.
ui.mon.dns_query_hint: Optional. Empty only checks that the server answers; with a name, the answer is checked too.
ui.mon.dns_qtype_hint: Enter a name to look up first.
ui.mon.dns_expect_hint: Optional: an address or value the answer must contain, e.g. 203.0.113.10.
ui.mon.group_hint: Pick an existing group ({groups}) or type a new name to create one.
ui.mon.group_hint_none: Type a name to create a group; monitors with the same group are shown together.
ui.ov.exit_idle: not checked: every internet target answers
ui.config.readonly: Read-only. Add and change monitors, channels and the rest on their pages; to edit the file itself, change it on the server and raise the revision — it is applied within seconds.
ui.config.help_readonly: Each line is “name [interval] IN TYPE target key=value…”; the full syntax is in docs/spec/monitors-conf.md.
ui.cfgissue.title: Setup problems
ui.cfgissue.no_channel: No notification channel yet: when something breaks, nobody is told.
ui.cfgissue.no_policy: The admin team has no channels and there are no system channels, so problems notify nobody.
ui.cfgissue.contacts: Recipient problems in channels: {n} (not in the contacts, left, or bouncing).
ui.set.dns_hint: Empty uses this host's settings (now: {list}). Separate several with commas; they are tried in order.
ui.set.exit_hint: Pinged only when an internet target fails, to tell whether this host can reach the internet. Default {addr}; empty turns it off.
ui.mon.select_first: Tick monitors in the list first
sys.outage_summary_ok: This host lost its network {from}–{to} ({duration}) and could not check anything meanwhile ({paused} monitors waited). Re-checked since: all fine.
sys.outage_summary_failing: This host lost its network {from}–{to} ({duration}) and could not check anything meanwhile ({paused} monitors waited). Re-checked since: {failing} still failing — {names}
ev.outage_summary: Local outage over ({duration_s}s): {affected} monitors affected, {failing} still failing after the re-check, {dropped} stale notices dropped
ev.outage_backdated: {monitors} failures began with the local outage and were taken back
ev.closed_local_network: Incident withdrawn: it began with this host's network outage
sys.digest_network_title: Network fault: {n} monitors affected — please contact the network team
sys.digest_segment: {n} monitors in {segment} fail at the network level at the same time: the segment, its switch or its uplink is the likely cause; the services may be fine.
sys.digest_dns: {n} monitors cannot resolve their names at the same time: DNS is the likely cause; the services may be fine.
sys.storage_failing: Writing to the data directory fails since {time} ({error}); check results and events are kept in memory and retried, {lost} were lost. Free some disk space or fix the file system.
ui.storage_failing: Results and events cannot be written to disk since {since} (full disk?). They are kept in memory and retried; {lost} were lost.
sys.hold_released: This host's network has looked down since {time} ({duration}). To be safe, Unagikuma no longer holds back the alerts of the {n} monitors it paused: they are checked and alerted normally again. If the network really is down, these alerts may be wrong.
sys.hold_note: Note: this host's network has looked down since {time}; this alert was released after the maximum hold time and may be wrong.
detail.cert_untrusted: certificate rejected: not issued by a trusted authority (self-signed?)
detail.cert_name: certificate rejected: issued for another name ({names})
detail.keyword_missing: keyword {kw} not found in the response
detail.keyword_unwanted: unwanted text {kw} found in the response
detail.ping_tcp_ok: answered on TCP port {port} in {ms} ms (ping not allowed here, checked over TCP)
detail.ping_tcp_unreachable: host unreachable (checked over TCP: ping not allowed here)
detail.ping_privilege: ping is not allowed for this process, and the host did not answer on TCP ports 443, 80 or 22. Allow ping: sysctl net.ipv4.ping_group_range="0 2147483647", or setcap cap_net_raw+ep on the binary
detail.udp_unreachable: nothing listens on that UDP port
detail.w_reflection: {kw} replies can be abused for reflection attacks; add authorized=yes if this is your own device
detail.w_secret: {k} looks like a password written in clear text; use ${secret:NAME}
detail.w_timeout: timeout {t} is not shorter than the interval {i}
detail.w_stateful: {kw} creates state on the target: interval raised to {i}
ui.uptime.so_far: Watched for only {pct} of this window so far: the figure covers that part only.
ui.audit.verify_ok: Intact: {n} entries, none changed, inserted or removed. Newest entry: {head}
msg.class.business: Service failure: the service answers, but not as expected. Its owner should look at it now.
msg.class.uncertain: Cannot be reached: the service, its host or the network path to it may be down. Check whether it answers from elsewhere.
msg.class.segment: Network failure: {n} monitors in {segment} fail at the network level together. The network team should look first; the services may be fine.
msg.class.local: Network failure on this side: the monitoring host's own network is failing, so this may not be the service. Sent because the hold was released.
sys.backstop_title: Alerts held back to avoid flooding you: {n}
sys.backstop_body: Total alerts: {n}. Monitors involved ({monitors}): {names}. The most severe:
pm.title: Incident #{id} report: {name}
pm.seg.lead_up: Before: changes in the previous 24 hours
pm.last_ok: last successful check before the failure
pm.no_changes: No configuration or operational changes were recorded.
pm.step.failed: {kind} alert could not be delivered to {to}
pm.step.held: held back as a local network outage from {from} to {to}
pm.step.released: hold released after {from}, judged normally again from {to}
pm.step.dropped: {kind} alert dropped: replaced by the outage summary
pm.step.backstop: {kind} alert folded into a digest (too many alerts in one minute)
pm.never_told: No problem alert was delivered to anyone.
pm.told_after: first alert delivered {after} after the failure was confirmed, to {to}
pm.reopened: it failed again shortly after recovering (times: {n})
pm.c.open: {monitor} has been failing since {since} and has not recovered yet.
pm.c.told: The first alert arrived {after} after the failure was confirmed ({total} after the first failed check).
pm.c.changed: The monitor's own configuration was changed in the 24 hours before (changes: {n}).
pm.c.live_unknown: Whether monitoring ran throughout can no longer be checked (detailed history has been cleaned up).
pm.c.live_gaps: Monitoring was interrupted (gaps: {n}, {total} in total): see below.
pm.live.no_gaps: No gaps: every check ran on time.
pm.live.unknown: The detailed check history for this period is no longer kept, so gaps cannot be shown.
pm.cov.depth.L3: Depth L3: the reply is read and its content checked.
pm.cov.depth.L2: Depth L2: any valid reply counts; the content is not checked.
pm.cov.depth.L1: Depth L1: only that the packet was not refused; a silent failure may go unseen.
pm.cov.depth.L0: Depth L0: only reachability is checked.
pm.cov.every: Every {interval}; {attempts} failed checks in a row before an alert; timeout {timeout}.
pm.cov.local: Checked from this server only: a failure of the path from here looks the same as a failure of the service.
pm.cov.limit: Anything this check does not ask for (other pages, other ports, data correctness) is not covered.
pm.cov.unknown: This monitor is no longer configured: what it checked cannot be shown.
sys.dns_summary_ok: This host's DNS resolver did not answer {from}–{to} ({duration}); the {paused} monitors checked by name waited. Re-checked since: all fine.
sys.dns_summary_failing: This host's DNS resolver did not answer {from}–{to} ({duration}); the {paused} monitors checked by name waited. Re-checked since: {failing} still failing — {names}
ui.mon.resume_skipped: Not resumed because their script is missing on some nodes: {names}. Resume them one by one from their page.
sys.title.master: The master is unreachable. Monitoring continues with the last configuration.
sys.resolved.master: The master is reachable. Configuration synchronization resumes.
sys.master_unreachable: The master is unreachable. Monitoring continues with the last configuration.
sys.peer_unreachable: This site cannot reach {node}. With two sites nobody can tell which side is cut off, so {node} is not reported down; both sites keep checking and alerting on their own.
sys.minority_title: Cannot reach the other nodes: their status is unknown
sys.minority: This node reaches only {reach} of {total} nodes, so it is in the minority and cannot tell whether {nodes} are down or it is cut off itself. Nothing is reported down from here; this site keeps checking and alerting on its targets.
sys.two_masters_title: Two masters of this cluster are running
sys.two_masters: Another master ({peer}, term {term}) is reachable. Only one master may run; promote or shut one down.
ui.rep.local_hint: Each site checks and alerts independently. Shared observations are informational only.
ui.rep.peers: Other nodes as seen from here
ui.verdict.down_hint: More than half of the cluster cannot reach this node.
ui.verdict.unreachable_hint: This node cannot reach it, but not enough nodes confirm it is down.
ui.verdict.unknown_hint: This node cannot reach more than half of the cluster, so it cannot judge the others.
ui.gw.title: Notification uplink
ui.audit.site_hint: Each site keeps its own audit chain; logs of other sites arrive here when they merge after a split.
ui.inc.site_hint: Recorded by another site while it checked on its own, merged here after the link came back.
ui.ha.promote_sync: The master is reachable: a final copy is taken first.
ui.ha.promote_nosync: The master cannot be reached: changes made there after the copy come back as a merge when it returns, and never overwrite newer data.
ui.sl.title: Site-local configuration
ui.sl.hint: Monitors, channels and policies for this site only, in the same format as the main configuration. Checked and alerted on here in every role; never sent to other nodes and never overwritten by the master's sync, a join or a promotion.
ui.sl.file_hint: File name in the data directory
ui.sl.howto: One monitor per line: a name, IN, the check type and the target. For example:
ui.sl.howto_more: Options and channels are written as in the main configuration. The $FILE line is added when you save. A short form such as ping 8.8.8.8 is answered with the full line to use.
ui.sl.err_record: is not a monitor line. Write: name IN TYPE target, for example router IN PING 192.168.1.1.
ui.sl.suggest: These lines read as short forms; write them like this:
ui.config.term_hint: The master term this version was written under; versions of different terms may have diverged.
ui.dv.title: Diverged configurations
ui.dv.hint: A replaced master kept a configuration different from the one this master took over with. It was not applied: compare it and carry over what you need by hand.
reason.inconclusive: Inconclusive: no reply, and the host does not answer either
reason.port_busy: Source port in use on this node
ui.mon.share_hint: The target is checked once; each monitor keeps its own thresholds, incidents and notifications.
ui.team.intro: Every monitor belongs to one team. Members see their teams' monitors; what they may do follows their account role. The built-in admin team owns the rest.
ui.team.unknown_hint: Add these user names under Users, or correct them.
ui.team.name_hint: The team's internal name in English letters, used in the configuration (team=…). It cannot be changed later.
ui.team.field_hint: The team that owns this monitor.
ui.dir.notify_hint: How the system reaches this person directly, for example as a team manager.
ui.dir.notify_none: Add an e-mail, SMS or voice channel under Channels first; then choose it here.
ui.dir.need_address: Enter at least one e-mail address or phone number.
ui.dir.need_notify: Choose at least one channel to reach this person through.
ui.user.contact_none_hint: Not linked to a contact. Link it in the contact's form (Alerts & notifications › Contacts › More › Login).
ui.dir.phone_odd: Check the length of: {list}. A Chinese mobile number has 11 digits; other numbers need the country code (+…). Saving is still allowed.
ui.dir.status_hint: On leave or moved: no alerts. Left: no alerts, and the linked login is disabled.
ui.dir.notify_auto: Reached through: {list}. Change this under More.
ui.dir.notify_auto_none: Add an e-mail address or a phone number so this person can be reached.
ui.dir.reach.no_channel: No way to reach them chosen
ui.dir.reach.no_address: Missing the address the channel needs
ui.dir.reach.channel_gone: The chosen channel no longer exists
ui.team.unreachable: {names} have no way to be reached yet: when every channel fails, they cannot be told.
ui.ch.program_hint: Found by itself (/usr/sbin/sendmail and the usual places); postfix, sendmail, exim, msmtp and the like all provide it. Set only for an unusual place.
ui.ch.from_sendmail_hint: May stay empty: the mail system then sends as this machine, as it does for Nagios.
ui.inc.archive: Historical snapshot; actions are sent to the source site
detail.push_site: PUSH requires exactly one receiving site
detail.config_read_only: configuration is read-only on this site
ui.import.adapter_intro: Choose one Checkmate monitors.json export or Gatus YAML file (HTTP subset, 1 MiB maximum). Unsupported items block apply. No accounts, tenants, alerts or environment variables are imported. Review every note before applying.
ui.wall.title: Wall screen
ui.wall.stale: No new data since {ago}: check the connection to the server
ui.wall.need_link: This wall screen needs a link
ui.wall.need_link_hint: An administrator can create one under Advanced › Appearance › Wall screen.
ui.look.wall_hint: Every monitor as a large hexagon, problems first, for a TV in the operations room. Read-only, refreshed every 10 seconds. Open it here, or create a link for a TV that has no login: it contains a read-only API token, which you can revoke under Advanced › API tokens.
ui.look.wall_link: Create a link for a TV
ui.look.wall_link_done: Link created. Open it on the TV; anyone with it can see monitor names and states.
ui.sum.title: Service summary
ui.sum.now_bad: {n} of {total} services have a problem right now
ui.sum.need_link: This summary needs you to sign in
ui.sum.need_link_hint: Sign in to the console first, then open it again.
ui.look.sum_hint: Availability, number of outages and recovery time over 7, 30 or 90 days, compared with the previous period, and the services that need attention. Read-only and printable; open it here while signed in.
ui.look.sum_link_done: Link created. Anyone with it can see service names, availability and incidents.
ui.notice.support_text: Text in place of “Powered by Unagikuma”
ui.notice.support_hint: Shown at the foot of every status page. Leave empty for the usual line.
ui.notice.support_locked: Changing this line needs a registered installation.
ui.team.members_hint: A ticked login sees only this team's monitors when it signs in, and acts on them as its role allows. Administrators always see everything.
ui.team.add_users_hint: There is no other login yet; add one under
ui.team.move_first: Move its monitors to another team first
ui.region.field_hint: The nodes that check it. Global: every node.
ui.region.intro: Regions group nodes. A monitor is checked by the nodes of its region; global, the default, is every node.
ui.region.no_nodes: Add nodes under Run mode first
ui.region.delete_confirm: Delete region {name}? Its {n} monitors move to global.
ui.user.admin_team_only: There is only the admin team: the user joins it.
ui.ch.system_hint: Receives system notices, and the problems of teams without a working channel.
ui.mon.mute_hint: Problems are recorded; nothing is sent.
ui.mon.system_channel_hint: Sent through the system channels instead of the team's.
ui.team.channels_hint: The first is the primary, the rest are backups. Without channels the system channels are used and the team's admins are told.
ui.team.mode.fallback: In order, stop at the first success
sys.left_out_body: Not sent to: {recipients}. E-mail and SMS go only to active contacts; see Alerts & notifications › Contacts.
ui.dir.tell_admins: Tell the team's administrators when recipients are left out (once a day per channel)
ui.dir.issue.inactive: {address} belongs to {person}, who is on leave or transferred: skipped
ui.mon.pause_relayed: Sent to the master: it takes effect on every node in a moment.
ui.report.team_receives: This team receives the daily report
ui.report.receiving_none: No team receives the daily report.
ui.report.opt_out_hint: Anyone can switch the report off for themselves under Alerts and notifications › Users.
ui.ch.test_ok_connection: Connection probe succeeded (does not prove real alert recipients are reachable)
ui.ch.test_filtered: {n} recipient(s) filtered by the active-contact whitelist; {kept} kept
ui.sys.ui_plaintext: This UI request used plain HTTP. Prefer a TLS reverse proxy or --tls-cert/--tls-key. Agent traffic already uses pinned TLS on the same port. Keep the listen address on a private network.
ui.ha.master_alive: The master {master} is still running. Taking over now makes two masters. To move the master role, hand over from the master (Settings › Nodes). Promote anyway only if that master is broken.
